data.narrative:
Zoo, a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jessie Frazelle, Jordan Noone, Jenna Bryant, and Hannah Bollar, has raised $35.5M to date. The robotics sector comp universe includes one public company (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private peers, among them Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI.

A stage-progression valuation framework was applied, using the $35.5M total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression. This method yielded an implied valuation of $89M. A peer-median approach was not applicable; while ten robotics and manufacturing companies exist in the broader comp set, insufficient same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier peers remain after narrow filtering (minimum three required for statistical reliability), precluding meaningful median derivation.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $75M to $102M, with a median of $89M. This range reflects extrapolation from a single applicable method and carries material uncertainty around both near-term funding trajectory and appropriate stage-specific multipliers for frontier robotics ventures. The absence of sufficient tightly-filtered peer data remains the primary constraint on precision; wider-sector comparables would require explicit discount or premium application not supported by current information.
